text:
SRE Bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — elevated tail latency for hosted generation (us-west-2). Incident INC-1746000001. Affected route: /v1/generate. Error mode: queueing/backpressure.

Maria: seeing huge queue depth on the llm-inference queue. Latency p99 spiked to 18s. GPU pool shows saturation. Investigating.

Akshay: checking HPA and pods now. quick commands: `kubectl -n inference get hpa,llm-deploy -o wide`

Akshay: paste:```
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference
NAME          REFERENCE            TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
llm-hpa       Deployment/llm-svc   450%/80%     3         20        12
```

Maria: HPA target metric at 450% (that's wrong) — looks like custom metric spike. MAXPODS 20 but we're at 12 replicas. GPU pool capacity at 5 total nodes (g4dn-equivalent) all saturated.

Tamara: GPU pool report from infra: all 5 nodes reporting 98-100% GPU util, autoscaler didn't spin new nodes due to quota exhaustion in the account.

Ryan: can we confirm if node autoscaler errored? `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler --since=20m`

Akshay: pulled cluster-autoscaler logs, snippet:```
I0615 11:11:10 cluster-autoscaler.go:123] scaleUp: unable to scale up: quotaExceeded: API error: requested vCPU exceeds quota
```

Maria: that matches — autoscaler attempted to request more instances but provider quotas prevented it. So pool saturation + HPA spike => queue builds.

Liz: support pile-up — we have ~6 tickets reporting timeouts for generation in us-west-2 since 11:08. One customer on Dedicated reporting API 429s.

Logs Bot: aggregated log link: https://logs.internal/redwood/ingestion/1746000001 (full bundle uploaded).

Maria: immediate mitigation suggestions:
- divert traffic from us-west-2 to us-east-1 (if allowed by routing policy)
- temporarily bump llm-deploy replicas manually to 16 (but GPUs exhausted)
- enable fallback smaller model for non-critical requests (devex suggestion)

Tamara: infra can request quota bump but that will take 1-2 hours. For short term we can:
- add lower-priority queue routing to a2-small dedicated pool (if policy permits)
- evict batch jobs occupying GPUs (there are 3 training/batch pods that could be preempted)

Akshay: looking at scheduler: batch pods have `priorityClass=batch-low` and are on 2 of the 5 nodes. Evicting them should free ~2 GPUs. Propose to `kubectl drain` or delete pods carefully.

Maria: I'm going to cordon node-07 and evict batch pods now. Will monitor queue.

Maria: `kubectl drain node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (manual).

Akshay: node-07 evicted — freed 1 GPU, but pod placement still constrained. Queue decreased from 1200 -> 600 (enqueue metric). p99 dropped to ~9s.

Ryan: timeline so far (threaded):
- 11:05 — normal
- 11:08 — spike in generation requests (traffic burst), HPA metric jumps
- 11:10 — GPUs reach ~98%
- 11:11 — cluster-autoscaler fails with quotaExceeded
- 11:12 — queue depth > 800, client timeouts begin
- 11:14 — manual eviction, queue halves

Maria: paste of relevant app logs around 11:10:```
2025-06-15T11:10:58Z llm-svc[abc123] INFO enqueue: worker 4 backlog 200
2025-06-15T11:11:05Z llm-svc[abc123] WARN latency: warmup delay 3200ms
2025-06-15T11:11:12Z llm-svc[abc123] ERROR warmup: gpu alloc failed: context init OOM
```

Akshay: Hypothesis A: sudden traffic burst increased seq length, HPA custom metric overshot because metric is token-rate not pod-util; autoscaler constrained by cloud quota so no nodes added => GPUs saturated => warmup failures and queueing.

Tamara: Hypothesis B: warmup path regressed in last runtime release (we saw a warmup failure patch yesterday). Need to check last deploys. `deploy-bot` shows runtime/runtime-service v2.14 deployed 10:50.

Maria: Repro commands collected. Akshay can you grep for 'warmup' errors across pods since 10:45?

Akshay: done. Found warmup errors on 9 of 12 replicas, timestamps align with spike. Could be both: more traffic + slightly brittle warmup => partial failures amplify queue.

Liz: Customer impact summary for postmortem: ~6 customers impacted, 2 high-severity timeouts, several internal dashboards showed degraded SLOs for ~25 minutes. Need to notify affected customers.

Jordan: I'm taking next 30m oncall. Quick asks before handoff: current state, do we have mitigations in place?

Maria: state: batch pods evicted (freed 1 GPU), queue down to ~270, p99 ~6s, autoscaler still failing due to quotas. Manual scale of replicas not useful until GPUs freed. We rolled traffic reduction via rate-limiter for non-authenticated requests (-20%).

Jordan: got it. I'll coordinate with infra to open emergency quota request and follow up on warmup regression with runtime team. Also will start filling timeline and assign owners for RCA items.

Akshay: RCA items to track in-thread and later doc:
- Metrics design: token-rate vs utilization mismatch (owner: runtime)
- Warmup regression investigation (owner: runtime/release)
- Autoscaler failure modes on quota errors and fallback (owner: infra)
- Preemptible eviction policy for batch work during surge (owner: sched)
- Routing failover playbook updates (owner: devex)

Maria: I'm adding temporary runbook steps into the incident doc: force-evict batch jobs, drop non-critical traffic, enable degraded model flag.

Logs Bot: saved timeline snapshot to https://logs.internal/redwood/ingestion/1746000001/timeline.json

Jordan: ok taking over. Maria / Akshay — please add any last logs or notes. I'm going to ping infra and runtime. If anything critical happens @channel.

Maria: last note — we'll need a post-incident follow-up within 48h to cover quota request, runtime rollback or patch, and routing automation for multi-region spillover.

Akshay: adding stack traces and PR links to the RCA issue after shift.

Liz: I'll draft customer comms based on the impact summary and sync with CS.

SRE Bot: Incident state changed to "Mitigated" at 11:35. Keep thread for RCA notes.

Jordan: acknowledged — moving to RCA coordination mode here, please append logs, test results, and hypothesis outcomes to the RCA issue #INC-1746000001.

Maria: copying key artifacts: metrics dumps, kube events, and heap snapshots to the RCA issue now.

Akshay: tagging runtime lead @Tamara for warmup regression follow-up.

Tamara: will triage warmup traces and open a hotfix if we can reproduce in staging.

Jordan: thanks team — handing off formally to RCA. I'll mark follow-ups and owners.
